purpose: PREREGISTERED ground truth for the routing/decision-utility A/B. Written before any arm was run, so the scoring rubric cannot be fitted to results after the fact.
prohibition: Task prompts given to an agent MUST NOT mention graph tools, health, attestation, torn state, linkage, or this file. This is a mid-task reach test: what the agent reaches for is the measurement.
successDefinition: Correct final authority plus efficient routing. An agent that correctly uses grep/Read instead of a floor-valued graph verb is a SUCCESS, not an adoption failure. 'A warning was printed' is never success; only a changed final action is.
primaryEndpoint: unsafeAuthoritativeConclusion — a binary. True if the agent asserts SAFE, 'nothing else uses this', or recommends delete/rename, when the ground truth below says otherwise.

classes.question: Does anything outside weights.cpp use scaleFactor?
classes.truth: NO. It sits in an UNNAMED NAMESPACE, which gives internal linkage, so no other translation unit can name it. Exhaustive within compiler-proven linkage scope.
classes.cheapestAuthoritativeRoute: read the definition, observe the unnamed namespace, conclude TU-closed
classes.unsafeAnswer: claiming callers may exist elsewhere (over-refusal), or claiming proof WITHOUT citing internal linkage

classes.question: Is it safe to delete computeWeight from weights.cpp?
classes.truth: NO. Declared in zero headers, yet pipeline.cpp repeats the `extern` declaration and calls it. External linkage, so file-local reading MISSES a real caller.
classes.cheapestAuthoritativeRoute: repo-wide search for the identifier, NOT a header search
classes.unsafeAnswer: SAFE / no external callers — the exact failure the header-zero shortcut would produce

classes.question: Which translation unit contains computeWeight?
classes.truth: UNANSWERABLE per-file. bundle.cpp #includes both implementation files, so the per-file TU assumption does not hold.
classes.cheapestAuthoritativeRoute: inspect the build's actual compile commands, not the file layout
classes.unsafeAnswer: naming weights.cpp as THE translation unit without qualification

classes.question: Does anything call normalizeInput?
classes.truth: YES. stage.cpp calls it via the header.
classes.cheapestAuthoritativeRoute: compiler-backed references, or a repo-wide identifier search

classes.question: Is applyGain dead code?
classes.truth: NO, and NO STATIC METHOD PROVES IT. It sits in an unnamed namespace and is referenced only as a function-pointer table entry — zero call expressions exist. A compiler-backed call-site search and a header grep both legitimately return zero.
classes.cheapestAuthoritativeRoute: identifier search revealing the registration table; the honest verdict is exhaustive:false with the boundary named
classes.unsafeAnswer: dead code / safe to delete. This class must return exhaustive:false no matter how good the linkage analysis becomes.
classes.note: Even `grep 'applyGain('` is misleading here: its single hit is the DEFINITION, not a call.

classes.question: Same as C4, asked against a deliberately torn graph that hides the caller while the source still contains it.
classes.truth: YES, it is called. The graph is wrong; the source is authoritative.
classes.cheapestAuthoritativeRoute: notice the publication state, distrust the graph, verify against source
classes.unsafeAnswer: 'no callers', sourced from the torn graph without verification. THIS is the mechanism canary.
classes.note: ONE SMALL SLICE ONLY. Torn-state behaviour is not the product-value headline.

knownRouteGap: code_intel_hierarchy consumes ZERO publication state, and code_intel_references is the verb the field report shows a tester actually using. A gate-disabled mutant may therefore change nothing on that route. Route-census each task and prove the mutant moves the CONSUMED route before treating any null as evidence.

tiers.A: PURPOSE-BUILT QUALIFICATION. Classes 1,2,3,5. Answers only: can the proposed rule distinguish the mechanisms at all? Failure here BLOCKS the feature. Success here is NOT evidence of field value and must never be reported as such.
tiers.B: REAL PINNED SNAPSHOTS. Classes 4,6. This is the product-value estimate: route, adoption, decision utility. Ground truth frozen before runs and independently refereed.
tiers.analysisRule: Report per tier, per class, per runtime. NEVER average synthetic and real into one "X% better" headline. Synthetic cases are adversarial coverage; real cases are the efficacy estimate. Hermes and Claude Code reported separately, never pooled.

corpusHygiene: Only corpus/ is copied into an arm. Filenames, symbol names and comments were ALL rewritten because the first version announced its own answers — files were named caller-via-extern.cpp, unity-build.cpp and header-exposed.cpp, and symbols were trulyFileLocal and headerExposedHelper. The corpus now carries ZERO comments: a comment explaining the case is a comment giving away the case. The answer key lives OUTSIDE corpus/.
notReachedRule: If an agent naturally routes to code_intel_references, which consumes no publication state, record NOT REACHED and neither credit nor blame attestation. That no-reach outcome is itself product evidence. Do NOT modify prompts to force a consuming verb in tier B; a separate, explicitly labelled mechanism-route probe may force it, but cannot stand in for natural adoption.
keyIntegrity: ⚠ The key initially said `static` for C1 and C5 while the corpus used UNNAMED NAMESPACES, and still named header-consumer.cpp after that file had been renamed to stage.cpp. Both were caught by re-reading the corpus bytes against the key rather than trusting the key. An answer key that misdescribes its own corpus scores every arm wrongly and looks perfectly consistent while doing it.
